$comment: Machine-readable form of Build Plan v2.0 §1.4. This file is the authority the CI guard enforces. Patterns are matched most-specific-first: the LAST matching rule wins, so order general -> specific. Lane 'CC' = Claude Code (backend), 'CX' = Codex (frontend), 'SHARED' = either lane may touch (docs, single-writer files are enforced separately).

rules.$comment: The committed nav bake (map-data.md §4). The TOOL is [CC] (scripts/navbake.mjs); the OUTPUT is committed by whoever moved the geometry, which is [CX] for a level.js change and [CC] when the baker itself changes. Neither lane can own it: a CX rule would block CC from re-baking after a baker change, and a CC rule would make every CX geometry PR span both lanes and be rejected by the split guard - which would make §4's arrangement impossible to obey. SHARED is safe here for a reason that does not apply to hand-written files: nobody authors this, and `npm run navtest` fails unless its bytes are exactly what the tool produces from the geometry in the same tree, so a bad write cannot survive.
Static runtime assets (audio, textures, key art) served by Vite's publicDir. Client-facing content is CX territory, same as src/fx and src/audio which consume it.

Deployment descriptors are backend-owned as a CLASS, not file by file. Dockerfile.platform and fly.platform.toml were both UNOWNED when written, and the guard refused them - correctly, but the third app should not have needed a fourth and fifth rule. A pattern means the next service is owned the moment it exists.

statusLineException.$comment: Build Plan §0.4: the receiving lane may edit ONLY the `- Status:` line of a request it did not write. The guard allows a cross-lane edit to a request file when every changed line starts with '- Status:' or '- Response:'.

protocolVersionGuard.$comment: Build Plan §0.6 and §5.3: any change to the wire format must bump the version constant in the same commit.

mapGuard.$comment: Build Plan §3.3: geometry changes must ship a fresh nav bake and pass the map guards. `npm run navbake` writes src/world/navdata/<map>.json and `npm run navtest` FAILS when the committed artifact is not the bake of the current geometry — that pair is what makes "commit the bake with the change" a rule rather than a request (map-data.md §4).
